channel.title: California Uzbek — Latest
channel.description: Independent analysis · Central Asia & world geopolitics

item.title: Law on the revised Uzbek alphabet signed on Uzbek Language Day
item.description: On 21 October — Uzbek Language Day — President Shavkat Mirziyoyev signed a law improving the Latin-based Uzbek alphabet. The revised alphabet will have 28 letters and one apostrophe; four letters will be written differently.

item.title: Why sexual-harassment cases are hard to track in Kazakhstan
item.description: An incident on an Astana bus again highlighted the legal gap in recording and tracking public sexual harassment in Kazakhstan. With no dedicated criminal provision, such cases are not separated out in the statistics.

item.title: Labour flow to Russia falls 13.2% while remittances reach $9.3 billion
item.description: The Central Bank's H1 2026 Labour Market Review: fewer citizens going to Russia, remittances rising, and destinations shifting towards Europe and East Asia.

item.title: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian: 'Muslims should unite rather than split into two camps'
item.description: In an Al Jazeera interview, Iran's president spoke about Muslim unity, his readiness to join a 'Mecca alliance', and regional security.

item.title: Iran says it shot down a US drone over the Strait of Hormuz; the claim is unverified
item.description: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said on 20 October they intercepted a US MQ-9 drone over the Strait of Hormuz — its claimed 54th US drone. The US did not confirm it; CENTCOM says the strait stays open to trade.

item.title: How bonds work: face value, coupon, yield and risks
item.description: A bond is a security through which a government or company borrows money and repays it with interest. This reference explains the key terms of a bond, the inverse relationship between price and yield, the types of bonds, the risks, and Uzbekistan's steps into the international bond market, on the basis of sources.

item.title: Google Pay officially launches in Uzbekistan
item.description: Google launched Google Pay and Google Wallet in Uzbekistan on 19 October at the C5+1 digital technologies session in Samarkand; the Central Bank is integrating Humo, Uzcard, Visa and Mastercard.

item.title: Uzbekistan signs the Artemis Accords on space exploration
item.description: Uzbekistan joined the US-led Artemis Accords in Samarkand on 19 October, becoming the 77th signatory; the document was signed by Foreign Minister Bakhtiyor Saidov.

item.title: Mirziyoyev calls for faster ID-card border crossings with Tajikistan
item.description: On 19 October President Shavkat Mirziyoyev urged speeding up a system that would let citizens cross the Uzbekistan–Tajikistan border with an internal ID card, citing growing trade, freight and close family ties.

item.title: Over 1.3 million citizens received free medicines in nine months
item.description: According to the Ministry of Health, more than 1.3 million citizens received free medicines under the reimbursement program in January–September 2026; the state reimbursed 248.2 billion soums.

item.title: How social-media algorithms and the "filter bubble" work: why your feed shows what it shows
item.description: The feed on Facebook, Instagram, YouTube, TikTok and X is sorted by an algorithm, not by time. This reference explains how an algorithmic feed works, the concepts of the "filter bubble" and the "echo chamber," what the research evidence actually says, and the European Union's new rules, on the basis of sources.

item.title: Remittances reach $18.9 billion: a chance to channel migrant money to women entrepreneurs
item.description: According to the Central Bank of Uzbekistan, remittances reached $18.9 billion in 2025; a program by IFAD, the EU and Hamkorbank aims to direct that money into rural small businesses.

item.title: The victims of repression and the rehabilitation of the Jadids: historical memory in the independence years (1991–2002)
item.description: After independence, Uzbekistan made the restoration of the memory of the Jadid reformers and the victims of Soviet repression a key part of reclaiming its national history. This article sets out the execution and rehabilitation of the Jadids and the creation of the days and complexes of remembrance, on the basis of sources.

item.title: Rubio's Samarkand remark revives the Russian-language debate — but the clip was out of context
item.description: A brief exchange involving US Secretary of State Marco Rubio in Samarkand reignited debate over Russian versus Uzbek. Kun.uz and Daryo found that the viral clip had been taken out of context.

item.title: The Uzbek diaspora in Canada: the making of a young but growing community
item.description: The Uzbek community in Canada is a young diaspora formed mainly after independence in 1991, to which a stream of ethnic Uzbeks from Afghanistan has been added. This article sets out the community's origins, its main streams, where it has settled and its figures, on the basis of sources.

item.title: Mirziyoyev awards the US Secretary of State and Special Envoy with state orders
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev presented US Secretary of State Marco Rubio with the Order 'For Outstanding Merits' and US Special Envoy Sergio Gor with the Order 'Friendship' in Samarkand.

item.title: Uzbekistan to establish Tashkent International Fashion Academy: specialists for five industries
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev signed Decree PP-378 on 16 October 2026. The new state higher-education institution is built on a joint programme of the Tashkent Institute of Textile and Light Industry and the Paris International Fashion Academy; classes begin in the 2026/2027 academic year.

item.title: Trump pauses Russia sanctions for 60 days: 72% of Uzbek remittances come from that country
item.description: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said President Donald Trump has paused sanctions and tariffs on Russia for 60 days. Russia remains the largest single source of remittances flowing into Uzbekistan.

item.title: Uzbekistan–UAE trade rises 40% as Masdar and AMEA Power agree to expand projects
item.description: At the first session of the fuel-and-energy Investors Council in Tashkent on 16 October, President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met Masdar CEO Mohamed Jameel Al Ramahi and AMEA Power Chairman Hussain Al Nowais; bilateral trade has grown 40% since the start of 2026.

item.title: How divorce (talaq) works in Islam: talaq, idda, khul' and the legal procedure
item.description: Talaq is the procedure for dissolving a marriage in Islam — permitted, but treated as a last resort. This reference explains the types of talaq, the idda (waiting period), khul' (divorce initiated by the wife), faskh (judicial dissolution) and the legal procedure in Uzbekistan, on the basis of sources and settled facts. The aim is not to give a fatwa but to clarify the basic concepts.

item.title: Collectivization and "dekulakization": the forced displacement of Uzbek peasants, 1929–1934
item.description: The Soviet collectivization that began in 1929 and the "dekulakization" policy (liquidating the kulaks as a class) led in the Uzbek SSR to the confiscation of land and property, the deportation of families and flight toward the border. This history article sets out the key dates, policies and consequences of the process on the basis of sources; disputed figures are flagged separately.

item.title: UAE re-enters the Yemen war: Saudi Arabia provides air cover as Houthis strike Riyadh
item.description: The United Arab Emirates has agreed to resume funding southern anti-Houthi forces in exchange for Saudi air support. Fighting in Yemen has intensified since the 2022 UN ceasefire collapsed in July.

item.title: English-language theatre in Tashkent: Script Theatre brings British comedy to the stage
item.description: Script Theatre, an independent amateur company in Tashkent, is staging English playwright Ray Cooney's farce 'Out of Order' entirely in English at Human House; every performance has sold out, yet the project has not reached break-even.

item.title: Russia proposes an updated collective security concept for the Gulf
item.description: At the ninth ministerial meeting of the Russia–GCC Strategic Dialogue in Bahrain, Sergey Lavrov put forward an updated Gulf security framework; the GCC urged Russia to press Iran to halt its attacks.

item.title: Houthi attacks put Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030 to the test
item.description: Houthi attacks on three Saudi airports killed more than 20 people and forced the kingdom's flagship investment summit into a remote format — a blow to Riyadh's goal of attracting $100 billion in annual foreign investment by 2030. The Uzbek link: Saudi Arabia's ACWA Power has invested more than $15 billion in Uzbekistan's energy sector.

item.title: Uzbekistan calls for peaceful conflict resolution at the OIC session in Baghdad
item.description: The 52nd session of the OIC Council of Foreign Ministers was held in Baghdad; Uzbekistan's delegation was led by First Deputy Foreign Minister Bakhromjon Aloyev.

item.title: What GDP, economic growth and recession are: a full reference
item.description: Gross domestic product (GDP) is the headline figure that measures the size of a country's economy. This reference explains what GDP is, the difference between nominal and real GDP, how economic growth is measured, what a recession is, and how these concepts apply to Uzbekistan's figures, on the basis of sources.

item.title: The establishment of diplomatic relations between Uzbekistan and the United States (1991–1992)
item.description: The United States recognized Uzbekistan's independence on 25 December 1991, diplomatic relations between the two states were established on 19 February 1992, and the U.S. Embassy in Tashkent opened on 16 March 1992. This history article sets out the exact dates of the process, the first ambassadors, and the context of Uzbekistan's international recognition, drawing on the U.S. Department of State and other official sources.

item.title: Koryo-saram: the deportation of Koreans to Uzbekistan (1937) and the formation of the Korean community
item.description: In the autumn of 1937 the Soviet authorities forcibly relocated the Koreans living in the Far East en masse to Central Asia — mainly to Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan. It was the first case in the USSR in which an entire people was deported solely on the basis of ethnicity. This history explainer sets out, on the basis of sources, the reasons for the deportation, its scale and the formation of the Korean (Koryo-saram) community in Uzbekistan.

item.title: How takaful (Islamic insurance) works: tabarru', wakala and mudarabah models
item.description: Takaful is a Shariah-compliant insurance system in which participants contribute to a common fund with the intention of mutual help (tabarru'). It is considered free of the riba (interest), gharar (excessive uncertainty) and maysir (gambling) elements that scholars identify in conventional commercial insurance. This explainer sets out what takaful is, the models it runs on, and its history, on the basis of sources.
